excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 15
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: For to prophesy and to cast out demons and to do great powers on earth is indeed a lofty and wonderful thing; yet whoever is found in all these does not obtain the heavenly kingdom unless he walks by keeping to the observation of the right and just path.

The Lord declares and says: “Many will say to me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name?’ And then I will say to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from me, you who work iniquity.’”
Work of righteousness is needed, that one may be able to deserve God the Judge; his precepts and warnings must be obeyed, that our merits may receive their wage.
latin: Nam et prophetare et daemonia excludere et virtutes magnas in terris facere sublimis utique et admirabilis res est, non tamen regnum coeleste consequitur, quisquis in his omnibus invenitur, nisi recti et iusti itineris observatione gradiatur. Denuntiat Dominus et dicit: Multi mihi dicent in illo die: Domine, Domine, nonne in tuo nomine prophetavimus et in tuo nomine daemonia exclusimus et in nomine tuo virtutes magnas fecimus? Et tunc dicam illis: Nunquam vos cognovi, recedite a me, qui operamini iniquitatem.
translator_notes: New English from locked Latin. Gifts without unity/obedience do not save — gifts under moral and ecclesial order.

excerpts.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
english: When those around Montanus and Alcibiades and Theodotus in Phrygia were then first putting out among many the opinion about prophesying — for very many other marvelous works of the divine gift were still at that time being performed in various churches, and this was giving many people faith that those men also prophesied — and since there was disagreement about the matters declared, again the brothers in Gaul set out their own judgment about these things also, a cautious and most orthodox one…
greek: Τῶν δ᾽ ἀμφὶ τὸν Μοντανὸν καὶ Ἀλκιβιάδην καὶ Θεόδοτον, περὶ τὴν Φρυγίαν ἄρτι τότε πρῶτον τὴν περὶ τοῦ προφητεύειν ὑπόληψιν παρὰ πολλοῖς ἐκφερομένων· πλεῖσται γὰρ οὖν καὶ ἄλλαι παραδοξοποιΐαι τοῦ θείου χαρίσματος εἰσέτι τότε κατὰ διαφόρους ἐκκλησίας ἐκτελούμεναι, πίστιν παρὰ πολλοῖς τοῦ κἀκείνους προφητεύειν παρεῖχον· καὶ δὴ διαφωνίας ὑπαρχούσης περὶ τῶν δεδηλωμένων, αὖθις οἱ κατὰ τὴν Γαλλίαν ἀδελφοί, τὴν ἰδίαν κρίσιν καὶ περὶ τούτων, εὐλαβῆ καὶ ὀρθοδοξοτάτην ὑποτάττουσιν.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: …knowing that still day by day some are being discipled into the name of his Christ and leaving the way of error, who also receive gifts, each as they are worthy, being enlightened through the name of this Christ: for one receives a spirit of understanding, another of counsel, another of strength, another of healing, another of foreknowledge, another of teaching, another of fear of God.

And I said to him: “Listen, sir… after Christ’s ascent into heaven it was prophesied that he would take us captive from error and give us gifts. And these are the words: ‘He ascended on high, he led captivity captive, he gave gifts to human beings.’ We who have received gifts from the Christ who ascended on high therefore show from the prophetic words that you… are without understanding…”
greek: γινώσκων ἔτι καθʼ ἡμέραν τινὰς μαθητευομένους εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπολείποντας τὴν ὁδὸν τῆς πλάνης, οἳ καὶ λαμβάνουσι δόματα ἕκαστος ὡς ἄξιοί εἰσι, φωτιζόμενοι διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ τούτου· ὁ μὲν γὰρ λαμβάνει συνέσεως πνεῦμα, ὁ δὲ βουλῆς, ὁ δὲ ἰσχύος, ὁ δὲ ἰάσεως, ὁ δὲ προγνώσεως, ὁ δὲ διδασκαλίας, ὁ δὲ φόβου θεοῦ. … μετὰ τὴν τοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνέλευσιν προεφητεύθη αἰχμαλωτεῦσαι αὐτὸν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τῆς πλάνης καὶ δοῦναι ἡμῖν δόματα. Εἰσὶ δὲ οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι· Ἀνέβη εἰς ὕψος, ᾐχμαλώτευσεν αἰχμαλωσίαν, ἔδωκε δόματα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις.
translator_notes: New English from Perseus/First1KGreek Dialogue. Living gifts after the Ascension: healing, foreknowledge, teaching, etc.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: For among us even until now there are prophetic gifts; from which you yourselves ought also to understand that what of old was in your nation has been transferred to us.

And just as there were also false prophets in the time of the holy prophets who arose among you, so among us now there are also many false teachers, whom our Lord foretold that we should guard against…

Ὅνπερ δὲ τρόπον καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐπὶ τῶν παρʼ ὑμῖν γενομένων ἁγίων προφητῶν ἦσαν, καὶ παρʼ ἡμῖν νῦν πολλοί εἰσι καὶ ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι, οὓς φυλάσσεσθαι προεῖπεν ἡμῖν ὁ ἡμέτερος κύριος…

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: And among us it is possible to see both females and males who have gifts from the Spirit of God. So it was not because he was lacking in power that it was prophesied the powers numbered by Isaiah would come upon him, but because they were no longer going to be beyond him.
greek: Καὶ παρʼ ἡμῖν ἔστιν ἰδεῖν καὶ θηλείας καὶ ἄρσενας, χαρίσματα ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ θεοῦ ἔχοντας. Ὥστε οὐ διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐνδεῆ δυνάμεως ἐπεπροφήτευτο ἐλεύσεσθαι ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς δυνάμεις τὰς κατηριθμημένας ὑπὸ Ἡσαΐου, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸ ἐπέκεινα μὴ μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι.

english: The Word does not say these numbered powers of the Spirit came upon him as though he lacked them, but as about to make their rest upon him — that is, to make an end in him — so that prophets would no longer arise in your nation according to the old custom, which you can also see with your eyes: for after him no prophet at all has arisen among you.
greek: Ταύτας τὰς κατηριθμημένας τοῦ πνεύματος δυνάμεις οὐχ ὡς ἐνδεοῦς αὐτοῦ τούτων ὄντος φησὶν ὁ λόγος ἐπεληλυθέναι ἐπʼ αὐτόν, ἀλλʼ ὡς ἐπʼ ἐκεῖνον ἀνάπαυσιν μελλούσας ποιεῖσθαι, τουτέστιν ἐπʼ αὐτοῦ πέρας ποιεῖσθαι, τοῦ μηκέτι ἐν τῷ γένει ὑμῶν κατὰ τὸ παλαιὸν ἔθος προφήτας γενήσεσθαι, ὅπερ καὶ ὄψει ὑμῖν ἰδεῖν ἔστι· μετʼ ἐκεῖνον γὰρ οὐδεὶς ὅλως προφήτης παρʼ ὑμῖν γεγένηται.

excerpts.author: John Chrysostom
english: Why then does it not happen now? … What then used to happen then? If someone was baptized, he immediately spoke in tongues — and not in tongues only, but many also prophesied, and some displayed still more powers.

For those coming from the idols, knowing nothing clearly and not raised on the old books, when baptized immediately received the Spirit; but they did not see the Spirit (for it is invisible), so the grace gave a perceptible proof of that working: one spoke at once in the Persian tongue, another in the Roman, another in the Indian, another in some other such language — and this made plain to outsiders that there was a Spirit in the one speaking.

And they had gifts, some lesser, some greater. Yet among them the gift of tongues was more than all — and this became a cause of schism for them, not from its own nature, but from the ungraciousness of those who received it.
greek: Τί δήποτε γὰρ τότε μὲν ἐγίνετο, νῦν δὲ οὐκέτι; … Τί οὖν τότε συνέβαινεν; Εἴ τις ἐβαπτίσατο, γλώσσαις εὐθέως ἐλάλει, καὶ οὐ γλώσσαις μόνον, ἀλλὰ πολλοὶ καὶ προεφήτευον, τινὲς δὲ καὶ ἑτέρας πλείους δυνάμεις ἐπεδείκνυντο. … καὶ ὁ μὲν τῇ Περσῶν, ὁ δὲ τῇ Ῥωμαίων, ὁ δὲ τῇ Ἰνδῶν, ὁ δὲ ἑτέρᾳ τινὶ τοιαύτῃ εὐθέως ἐφθέγγετο γλώσσῃ· καὶ τοῦτο ἐφανέρου τοῖς ἔξωθεν, ὅτι πνεῦμα ἐστιν ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ φθεγγομένῳ. … καὶ χαρίσματα δὲ εἶχον, οἱ μὲν ἐλάττονα, οἱ δὲ μείζονα. Πλέον δὲ πάντων τὸ τῶν γλωσσῶν ἦν παρ’ αὐτοῖς χάρισμα. Καὶ τοῦτο αἴτιον σχίσματος αὐτοῖς ἐγένετο, οὐ παρὰ τὴν οἰκείαν φύσιν, ἀλλὰ παρὰ τὴν ἀγνωμοσύνην τῶν εἰληφότων.
translator_notes: New English from Field 1847 Greek OCR (cleaned). Landmark 4th-c. claim: baptismal tongues/prophecy were then common; Chrysostom asks why not now — Explore rupture toward later cessation talk.

excerpts.author: John Chrysostom
english: Therefore they also received discernings of spirits, so as to discern and know who speaks by a pure spirit and who by an unclean one. For it was not possible to give proof of the things said on the spot — prophecy does not furnish the test of its own truth at the time it is spoken, but at the time of the outcome…

And the prophet is not like the diviner, but with sober mind and self-control and composure, knowing what he utters, he says everything. So even before the outcome you may recognize from this the diviner and the prophet.

Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ αὐτόθεν οὐκ ἦν παρασχεῖν τῶν λεγομένων τὴν ἀπόδειξιν· προφητεία γὰρ οὐκ ἐν τῷ καιρῷ, ᾧ λέγεται, ἀλλ’ ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τῆς ἐκβάσεως παρέχεται τῆς οἰκείας ἀληθείας τὸν ἔλεγχον… Ὁ δὲ προφήτης οὐχ οὕτως, ἀλλὰ μετὰ διανοίας νηφούσης καὶ σωφροσύνης καὶ καταστάσεως, καὶ εἰδὼς ἃ φθέγγεται, ἅπαντά φησιν. Ὥστε καὶ πρὸ τῆς ἐκβάσεως κἀντεῦθεν γνώριζε τὸν μάντιν καὶ τὸν προφήτην.

excerpts.citation: Eusebius — Church History 5.17 (anonymous vs Montanist ecstasy)
excerpts.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
english: …in which [writing] he shows that a prophet ought not to speak in ecstasy… Going further in the same place he lists those who have prophesied according to the New Covenant, among whom he numbers a certain Ammia and Quadratus, saying: But the false prophet is in a kind of ecstasy, which is followed by license and fearlessness — beginning from voluntary ignorance and ending in involuntary madness of soul, as was said before. In this manner they will be able to show neither any prophet of the Old nor of the New who was borne by the Spirit — neither Agabus nor Judas nor Silas nor the daughters of Philip, nor Ammia in Philadelphia nor Quadratus, nor if there are any others who do not belong to them…
greek: ἐν ᾧ ἀποδείκνυσιν περὶ τοῦ μὴ δεῖν προφήτην ἐν ἐκστάσει λαλεῖν… ὑποκαταβὰς δ’ ἐν ταὐτῷ τοὺς κατὰ τὴν καινὴν διαθήκην προπεφητευκότας καταλέγει, ἐν οἷς καταριθμεῖ Ἀμμίαν τινὰ καὶ Κοδρᾶτον, λέγων οὕτως· ἀλλ’ ὅ γε ψευδοπροφήτης ἐν παρεκστάσει, ᾧ ἕπεται ἄδεια καὶ ἀφοβία, ἀρχομένου μὲν ἐξ ἑκουσίου ἀμαθίας, καταστρέφοντος δὲ εἰς ἀκούσιον μανίαν ψυχῆς, ὡς προείρηται. τοῦτον δὲ τὸν τρόπον οὔτε τινὰ τῶν κατὰ τὴν παλαιὰν οὔτε τῶν κατὰ τὴν καινὴν πνευματοφορηθέντα προφήτην δεῖξαι δυνήσονται, οὔτε Ἄγαβον οὔτε Ἰούδαν οὔτε Σίλαν οὔτε τὰς Φιλίππου θυγατέρας, οὔτε τὴν ἐν Φιλαδελφίᾳ Ἀμμίαν οὔτε Κοδρᾶτον, οὔτε εἴ δή τινας ἄλλους μηδὲν αὐτοῖς προσήκοντας…

excerpts.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
english: …his true disciples, having received grace from him, perform it for the benefit of the rest of humankind, each as he has received the gift from him. For some drive out demons firmly and truly, so that those cleansed from the evil spirits often themselves believe and are in the church; others have foreknowledge of things to come and visions and prophetic utterances; others heal the sick by laying on of hands and restore them to health; and, as we said, the dead have been raised and have remained with us for a fair number of years — and what more? One cannot number the gifts which the church throughout the whole world has received from God in the name of Jesus Christ crucified under Pontius Pilate, and which she performs each day for the benefit of the nations, neither deceiving anyone nor taking money…
greek: δι’ ὃ καὶ ἐν τῷ ἐκείνου ὀνόματι οἱ ἀληθῶς αὐτοῦ μαθηταί, παρ’ αὐτοῦ λαβόντες τὴν χάριν ἐπιτελοῦσιν ἐπ’ εὐεργεσίᾳ τῇ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀνθρώπων, καθὼς εἷς ἕκαστος τὴν δωρεὰν εἴληφεν παρ’ αὐτοῦ. οἱ μὲν γὰρ δαίμονας ἐλαύνουσιν βεβαίως καὶ ἀληθῶς, ὥστε πολλάκις καὶ πιστεύειν ἐκείνους αὐτοὺς τοὺς καθαρισθέντας ἀπὸ τῶν πονηρῶν πνευμάτων καὶ εἶναι ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, οἱ δὲ καὶ πρόγνωσιν ἔχουσιν τῶν μελλόντων καὶ ὀπτασίας καὶ ῥήσεις προφητικάς, ἄλλοι δὲ τοὺς κάμνοντας διὰ τῆς τῶν χειρῶν ἐπιθέσεως ἰῶνται καὶ ὑγιεῖς ἀποκαθιστᾶσιν, ἤδη δέ, καθὼς ἔφαμεν, καὶ νεκροὶ ἠγέρθησαν καὶ παρ’ ἡμῖν ἔτεσιν ἱκανοῖς, καί, τί γάρ; οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμὸν εἰπεῖν τῶν χαρισμάτων ὧν κατὰ παντὸς τοῦ κόσμου ἡ ἐκκλησία παρὰ θεοῦ λαβοῦσα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ σταυρωθέντος ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου ἑκάστης ἡμέρας ἐπ’ εὐεργεσίᾳ τῇ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιτελεῖ, μήτε ἐξαπατῶσά τινας μήτε ἐξαργυριζομένη…

excerpts.author: Didache
english: But let every apostle who comes to you be received as the Lord. Yet he shall not stay except one day; if there is need, also the next; but if he stays three days, he is a false prophet. And when the apostle goes out, let him take nothing except bread until he lodges; but if he asks for money, he is a false prophet.

excerpts.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
english: …of whom some crept through Asia and Phrygia like venomous reptiles, boasting of Montanus as the Paraclete, and of the women from him, Priscilla and Maximilla, as having become prophetesses of Montanus.

english: But the Phrygians, taking the beginnings of their heresy from a certain Montanus and Priscilla and Maximilla, thinking the women to be prophetesses and Montanus a prophet, suppose that they speak rightly about the origin and fashioning of the whole, and they have not taken up things about Christ in a foreign way; yet together with what was said before they go astray, attending to their words above the Gospels, and appointing new and strange fasts.
greek: Οἱ δὲ Φρύγες ἐκ Μοντανοῦ τινος καὶ Πρισκίλλης καὶ Μαξιμίλλης τὰς ἀρχὰς τῆς αἱρέσεως λαβόντες, προφήτιδας τὰ γύναια νομίζοντες καὶ προφήτην τὸν Μοντᾶνον, τὰ δὲ περὶ τῆς τοῦ παντὸς ἀρχῆς καὶ δημιουργίας ὀρθῶς λέγειν νομίζουσι, καὶ τὰ περὶ τὸν Χριστὸν οὐκ ἀλλοτρίως προσειλήφασιν, σὺν δὲ τοῖς προειρημένοις σφάλλωνται, ὧν τοῖς λόγοις ὑπὲρ τὰ εὐαγγέλια προσέχοντες πλανῶνται, νηστείας καινὰς καὶ παραδόξους ὁρίζοντες.

excerpts.citation: Basil of Caesarea — On the Holy Spirit (distribution of gifts / 1 Cor 12)
excerpts.author: Basil of Caesarea
english: Is the ordering of the church not clearly and without contradiction worked through the Spirit? For he himself, it says, gave to the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then powers, then gifts of healings, helps, governances, kinds of tongues. For this is the order arranged according to the division of the gifts from the Spirit.

…and there are distributions of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are distributions of ministries, but the same Lord; and there are distributions of workings, but the same God who works all things in all. But all these, it says, the one and the same Spirit works, distributing to each one individually as he wills.
greek: Ἐκκλησίας διακόσμησις οὐχὶ σαφῶς καὶ ἀναντιρρήτως διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος ἐνεργεῖται; Αὐτὸς γὰρ ἔδωκε, φησί, τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ πρῶτον ἀποστόλους, δεύτερον προφήτας, τρίτον διδασκάλους, ἔπειτα δυνάμεις, ἔπειτα χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων, ἀντιλήψεις, κυβερνήσεις, γένη γλωσσῶν. Αὕτη γὰρ ἡ τάξις κατὰ τὴν διαίρεσιν τῶν ἐκ τοῦ Πνεύματος δωρεῶν διατέτακται.

Διαιρέσεις γάρ, φησί, χαρισμάτων εἰσί, τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ Πνεῦμα· καὶ διαιρέσεις διακονιῶν εἰσιν, ὁ δὲ αὐτὸς Κύριος· καὶ διαιρέσεις ἐνεργημάτων εἰσίν, ὁ δὲ αὐτὸς Θεός, ὁ ἐνεργῶν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι. Ταῦτα δὲ πάντα, φησίν, ἐνεργεῖ τὸ ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ Πνεῦμα, διαιροῦν ἰδίᾳ ἑκάστῳ καθὼς βούλεται.
translator_notes: New English from Migne PG 32 OCR, cleaned where OCR systematically confuses κ/χ (noted). Re-check against a critical DSS edition before source_verified.
Joins Nicene Spirit-theology to 1 Cor 12 church order: gifts + offices as Spirit’s distribution.
notes: Wave 2026-09-10 post-Nicene (~375).

excerpts.author: Augustine of Hippo
english: Likewise, what I said — “Those miracles were not permitted to last into our times, lest the soul always seek visible things, and the human race grow cold by habit toward things at whose novelty it once burned” — is true in a sense. For it is not still the case that when hands are laid on the baptized they receive the Holy Spirit so as to speak in the tongues of all nations, nor that the sick are still healed by the shadow of Christ’s passing preachers, and if any such things were done then, it is clear they later ceased.

But what I said must not be taken to mean that now no miracles are believed to be done in Christ’s name. For I myself, when I wrote that very book, already knew that a blind man had been given sight at Milan at the bodies of the martyrs in that city, and not a few other things of the sort that happen so many even in these times that we can neither know them all nor enumerate those we do know.
latin: Item quod dixi: Nec miracula illa in nostra tempora durare permissa sunt, ne anima semper visibilia quaereret, et eorum consuetudine frigesceret genus humanum, quorum novitate flagravit, verum est quidem; non enim nunc usque, cum manus imponitur baptizatis, sic accipiunt Spiritum Sanctum, ut loquantur linguis omnium gentium, aut nunc usque ad umbram transeuntium praedicatorum Christi sanantur infirmi, et si qua talia tunc facta sunt, quae postea cessasse manifestum est. Sed non sic accipiendum est quod dixi, ut nunc in Christi nomine fieri miracula nulla credantur. Nam ego ipse, quando istum ipsum librum scripsi, ad Mediolanensium corpora martyrum in eadem civitate caecum illuminatum fuisse iam noveram et alia nonnulla, qualia tam multa etiam istis temporibus fiunt, ut nec omnia cognoscere nec ea quae cognoscimus, enumerare possimus.
translator_notes: New English from Archive OCR of Retractationes. Core Latin hinge for 0–800 map: baptismal tongues/Acts-style signs ceased; other miracles in Christ’s name still happen.

excerpts.author: Augustine of Hippo
english: On the miracles which were done so that the world might believe in Christ, and which do not cease to be done when the world has believed. “Why,” they ask, “do those miracles you preach as having been done not happen now?” I could indeed say they were needed before the world believed, so that the world might believe…

For even now miracles are done in his name, whether through his sacraments or through the prayers or memorials of his saints; but they are not made famous with the same clarity so as to be celebrated with as great a glory as those. For the canon of the sacred writings… makes those be recited everywhere… but these, wherever they happen, are known there scarcely by the whole city…
latin: De miraculis, quae ut mundus in Christum crederet facta sunt et fieri mundo credente non desinunt. Cur, inquiunt, nunc illa miracula, quae praedicatis facta esse, non fiunt? Possem quidem dicere necessaria fuisse, priusquam crederet mundus, ad hoc ut crederet mundus…

Nam etiam nunc fiunt miracula in eius nomine, sive per sacramenta eius sive per orationes vel memorias sanctorum eius; sed non eadem claritate inlustrantur, ut tanta quanta illa gloria diffamentur. Canon quippe sacrarum litterarum… illa facit ubique recitari… haec autem ubicumque fiunt, ibi sciuntur vix a tota ipsa civitate…
translator_notes: New English from Dombart OCR. Chapter title itself answers: miracles do not cease after the world believes — but publicity differs from apostolic-age signs.

excerpts.citation: Cyril of Jerusalem — Catechetical Lecture on the Holy Spirit (Simon Magus / Pentecost)
excerpts.author: Cyril of Jerusalem
excerpts.locus: Catech. 16/17 (PG 33; Spirit lecture; edition numbering varies)
english: …was this not done when the Holy Spirit came down on the day of Pentecost? Why was Simon the Magician condemned? Was it not because he came to the apostles and said, “Give me also this authority, that on whomever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Spirit”? For he did not say, “Give me also fellowship of the Holy Spirit,” but “authority,” so that he might sell to others what cannot be sold, which he himself did not possess.
greek: …καταβάντος ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῆς Πεντηκοστῆς τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος; Διὰ τί κατεκρίθη Σίμων ὁ Μάγος; ἆρ’ οὐ προσελθὼν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις καὶ εἰπών· Δότε κἀμοὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην, ἵνα ᾧ ἂν ἐπιθῶ τὰς χεῖρας, λαμβάνῃ Πνεῦμα ἅγιον; Οὐ γὰρ εἶπε, Δότε κἀμοὶ Πνεύματος ἁγίου κοινωνίαν, ἀλλ’ ἐξουσίαν, ἵνα ἄλλοις πιπράσκῃ τὸ ἄπρατον, ὃ αὐτὸς μὴ ἐκέκτητο.
translator_notes: New English from PG 33 OCR (cleaned κ/χ OCR noise). Spirit’s gift is free κοινωνία, not purchasable ἐξουσία — order rule for charismata.

excerpts.citation: Cyril of Jerusalem — Catechetical Lecture on the Holy Spirit (against Manes as Paraclete)
excerpts.author: Cyril of Jerusalem
english: The most impious Manes… dared to say that he himself was the Paraclete whom Christ promised to send. But the Savior, knowing beforehand, said to the apostles: “You stay in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.” What then? Were the apostles who died two hundred years ago waiting for Manes until they should be clothed with the power? And will anyone dare to say they were not from then on full of the Holy Spirit? And it is written that then they laid on hands and they received the Holy Spirit.
greek: ὁ δυσσεβέστατος Μάνης… ἐτόλμησέ τε εἰπεῖν, ὅτι αὐτὸς εἴη ὁ Παράκλητος, ὃν ἐπηγγείλατο Χριστὸς ἀποστέλλειν. Ἀλλ’ ὁ Σωτὴρ προειδὼς εἶπε τοῖς ἀποστόλοις· Ὑμεῖς δὲ καθίσατε ἐν τῇ πόλει Ἱερουσαλήμ, ἕως οὗ ἐνδύσησθε ἐξ ὕψους δύναμιν. Τί οὖν ἄρα οἱ τελευτήσαντες ἀπόστολοι ἀπὸ διακοσίων ἐτῶν ἐξεδέχοντο τὸν Μάνην, ἕως ἂν ἐνδύσωνται τὴν δύναμιν; καὶ τολμήσει τις εἰπεῖν, ὅτι οὐκ ἦσαν ἔκτοτε πλήρεις ἁγίου Πνεύματος; Καὶ μὴν γέγραπται, ὅτι Τότε ἐπετίθεσαν τὰς χεῖρας, καὶ ἐλάμβανον Πνεῦμα ἅγιον.
translator_notes: New English from PG 33 OCR cleaned. Same Paraclete-monopoly pattern as Montanism — gift already given at Pentecost/hand-laying.

added_allusions.reason: Stay in Jerusalem until clothed with power.

notes: Wave 2026-09-10. Mentions Montanists earlier in same lecture.

excerpts.author: Gregory the Great
english: If we attend to visible things, we must believe so; but if we weigh invisible things, it is clear that it is a greater miracle to convert a sinner by the word of preaching and the comfort of prayer than to raise a dead body in the flesh. For in the one case flesh is raised that will die again; in the other a soul that will live forever. … The Lord raised Lazarus in the flesh; but he raised Saul in the mind.
latin: Si visibilia attendimus, ita necesse est ut credamus; si vero invisibilia pensamus, nimirum constat, quia majus est miraculum praedicationis verbo atque orationis solatio peccatorem convertere, quam carne mortuum resuscitare. In isto enim resuscitatur caro iterum moritura, in illo vero anima in aeternum victura. … Lazarum quippe … carne Dominus suscitavit; Saulum vero resuscitavit in mente.
translator_notes: New English from PL 77 OCR. Orders miraculous signs under pastoral conversion — late-antique bridge toward medieval gift talk.

excerpts.author: Gregory the Great
english: Recently in the province of Samnium a certain venerable man named Mena lived a solitary life… He possessed almost nothing for his use except a few beehives. When a certain Lombard wanted to plunder them, he was first corrected by that man’s word, and at once was tormented by an evil spirit before his feet. From this it came about that, as among all the inhabitants, so also among that barbarian people, his name was held famous.
latin: Nuper in Samnii provincia quidam venerabilis vir, Menas nomine, solitariam vitam ducebat… Hic itaque nihil ad usum suum aliud, nisi pauca apum vascula possidebat. Huic cum Langobardus quidam… prius ab eodem viro verbo correptus est, et mox per malignum spiritum ante ejus vestigia vexatus. Qua ex re factum est ut sicut apud omnes incolas, ita etiam apud eamdem barbaram gentem ejus celebre nomen haberetur.
translator_notes: New English from PL 77 OCR. Living sign-power under episcopal storytelling — gifts-as-miracles still claimed ~594.

excerpts.author: Augustine of Hippo
english: Is the Holy Spirit not given now, brothers? Whoever thinks that is not worthy to receive him. He is given even now. Why then does no one speak in the tongues of all nations, as those filled with the Holy Spirit then used to speak? Why? Because what that signified has been fulfilled… The church then was in one house; it received the Holy Spirit: it was in a few people, yet it was in the tongues of the whole world. … For that the small church then spoke in the tongues of all nations — what is that, except that this great church from the rising of the sun to its setting speaks in the tongues of all nations? What was promised then is being fulfilled now.

Let no one say: “I have received the Holy Spirit; why do I not speak in the tongues of all nations?” … What the soul is to the body of a man, that the Holy Spirit is to the body of Christ, which is the church… in some saints he works miracles, in others he speaks truth… but they live together. A amputated member does not keep the soul — so a Christian cut off as a heretic is not followed by the Spirit.
latin: Numquid modo, fratres, non datur Spiritus Sanctus? Quisquis hoc putat, non est dignus accipere. Datur et modo. Quare ergo nemo loquitur linguis omnium gentium, sicut loquebatur qui tunc Spiritu Sancto implebatur? Quare? Quia quod illud significabat, impletum est… Ecclesia tunc in una domo erat, accepit Spiritum Sanctum: in hominibus paucis erat, in linguis totius orbis erat… Nam quod illa Ecclesia parva linguis omnium gentium loquitur, quid est, nisi quod Ecclesia ista magna a solis ortu usque ad occasum linguis omnium gentium loquitur? Modo impletur quod tunc promittebatur.

Nemo ergo dicat: Accepi Spiritum Sanctum; quare non loquor linguis omnium gentium? … Quod autem est anima corpori hominis, hoc est Spiritus Sanctus corpori Christi, quod est Ecclesia… in aliis sanctis facit miracula, in aliis sanctis loquitur veritatem… Sed… praecisum amittit vitam. Sic et homo christianus catholicus est, dum in corpore vivit; praecisus haereticus factus est, membrum amputatum non sequitur spiritus.
translator_notes: New English from augustinus.it Latin (cleaner than PL OCR). Typological answer to Chrysostom’s “why not now?”: Spirit still given; individual all-nations tongues fulfilled in the church’s worldwide speech.

added_allusions.reason: Witnesses to the ends of the earth.

notes: Follow-up from Augustine fetch agent 2026-09-10.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: Be shrewd as the serpent in everything, and forever innocent as the dove. That is why you are both fleshly and spiritual: so you can deal gently with what shows before people’s faces, and ask for the unseen to be shown to you — that you may lack nothing and overflow with every gift.
greek: φρόνιμος γίνου ὡς ὁ ὄφις ἐν ἅπασιν καὶ ἀκέραιος εἰς ἀεὶ ὡς ἡ περιστερά. διὰ τοῦτο σαρκικὸς εἶ καὶ πνευματικός, ἵνα τὰ φαινόμενά σου εἰς πρόσωπον κολακεύῃς· τὰ δὲ ἀόρατα αἴτει ἵνα σοι φανερωθῇ, ὅπως μηδενὸς λείπῃ καὶ παντὸς χαρίσματος περισσεύῃς.
translator_notes: New English from locked Greek (middle recension). παντὸς χαρίσματος = every gift/charism — bishop charged to abound in gifts while shepherding visibly and asking for the unseen.
κολακεύῃς kept as gentle dealing with what appears before the face (not empty flattery as the point).
notes: gifts-mine 2026-09-12: gifts with episcopal office (charismata under ordered ministry).
